question:
A 27-year-old marathon trainee presents with a one-week history of lumbosacral back pain that forced
him to discontinue his training. He reports experiencing right-sided lower back and buttock tightness,
with symptoms exacerbating during sit-to-stand transitions. Considering the most probable diagnosis,
which combination of osteopathic findings would you most likely encounter in this patient's
examination? Answer Choices: (A) Positive straight leg raise test with radicular symptoms (B) Positive
FAIR test with sciatic nerve compression symptoms (C) Positive piriformis stretch test with contralateral
hip rotation (D) Positive Thomas test and positive pelvic shift test to the ipsilateral side as the
dysfunction (E) Positive Patrick's test with ipsilateral sacroiliac joint tenderness (F) Negative Thomas
test and negative pelvic shift test (G) Positive Thomas test and positive pelvic shift test to the
contralateral side of the dysfunction (H) Positive Ober test with limited hip adduction (I) Tender point
lateral to ASIS (J) Positive FABER test with decreased range of motion bilaterally
 A. Positive FAIR test with sciatic nerve compression symptoms
B. Positive Patrick's test with ipsilateral sacroiliac joint tenderness
C. Positive Thomas test and positive pelvic shift test to the ipsilateral side as the dysfunction
D. Positive straight leg raise test with radicular symptoms
E. Negative Thomas test and negative pelvic shift test
F. Positive piriformis stretch test with contralateral hip rotation

G. Tender point lateral to ASIS
H. Positive Ober test with limited hip adduction
I. Positive FABER test with decreased range of motion bilaterally
J. Positive Thomas test and positive pelvic shift test to the contralateral side of the dysfunction
